title: Accumulators explained: why the odds multiply, and so does the margin

scenes.say: An accumulator is one bet on several selections, and every one has to win. The odds multiply, and so does the bookmaker's margin.
scenes.caption: An accumulator is one bet on several selections, and every one has to win. The odds multiply, and so does the bookmaker's margin.

visual.title: The odds multiply, and so does the margin

scenes.say: Each win rolls everything on to the next: five pounds becomes ten, then eighteen, then twenty-seven, then sixty-seven pounds fifty.
scenes.caption: Each win rolls everything on to the next: £5 becomes £10, then £18, then £27, then £67.50.

scenes.say: The quick way: multiply your stake by every decimal price. Five, times two, times one point eight, times one point five, times two point five, is sixty-seven pounds fifty, your stake included. Lose any one selection, and the whole bet loses.
scenes.caption: The quick way: multiply your stake by every decimal price. £5 × 2.00 × 1.80 × 1.50 × 2.50 = £67.50, your stake included. Lose any one selection, and the whole bet loses.

scenes.say: If a match is postponed, that selection is usually void, and the bet carries on without it at lower odds. Drop the selection at one point eight, and it's settled as a treble: thirty-seven pounds fifty.
scenes.caption: If a match is postponed, that selection is usually void, and the bet carries on without it at lower odds. Drop the selection at 1.80, and it's settled as a treble: £37.50.

lines.text: Some special bets are voided entirely: check the rules

scenes.say: Every price includes the bookmaker's margin, and in an accumulator you pay it on every selection. With a five per cent margin on each, ten pounds on a single gets back nine pounds fifty-two on average. A four-fold gets back eight pounds twenty-three. An eight-fold, six pounds seventy-seven.
scenes.caption: Every price includes the bookmaker's margin, and in an accumulator you pay it on every selection. With a 5% margin on each, £10 on a single gets back £9.52 on average. A four-fold gets back £8.23. An eight-fold, £6.77.
